utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: As you are here, it may be a good idea if we treat this as a Status Conference so that time will commence for the next one as from today. If there's anything you wish to raise, you are welcome to do so. If you think of something later, not having received any warning of this, then certainly you may make an application by the way of motion in the usual way. At the present time, General Talic is proceeding with his application for a separate trial, and the English translation of his document arrived this morning. Hopefully now that the vacation is over, the translation services will be able to keep up with their promise to do these matters speedily. The other matter which is outstanding, though, from the point of view of General Talic is his motion to dismiss the previous indictment. Are you able to say, Mr. Pitron, whether you propose to proceed with that, in some way transposing it to the amended indictment, or are you in a position where you realise that you are unlikely to get very far with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have three things that I wish to say in relation to this question. The first is the following: First of all, I have not received a French translation yet of the document dated the 5th of January, 2000 requesting me to state whether I wish to continue with my motion related to the first indictment. So I read the document of the 5th of January, I read it in the English language, and if I understood it correctly, it seemed to me that you were asking me to continue, for the motion to proceed, that is. My second objection would be the following: I am in a bit of an embarrassing position because now I really do not know whether the amended indictment fully annuls and replaces the previous indictment, or is it simply an addition to the previous indictment? Of course, depending on that, that is to say, whether the first indictment should be taken into account or not, my position will have to be based on that. My third point: In view of your document dated the 5th of January, 2000, you are asking me to tell you whether I shall proceed in connection with the rulings of the Appeals Chamber in the Brdjanin case. I believe that it is not for me to personally state my views on that which this Tribunal has to say in the Talic case in relation to what the Tribunal concluded in the Brdjanin case. So I abide by my first motion related to the first indictment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, in answer to your first question, if you understood that document, albeit in the English version, as inviting you to continue, that is wrong. All that the Trial Chamber was asking was whether you intended to proceed. As to your second point, the amended indictment does, indeed, replace the original indictment. The original indictment is no longer relevant to the trial. As to your third statement, I'm not sure whether you are saying that you do not wish to state your own views or whether your own views are you wish to proceed. So I suggest we wait until you have received a French translation of the document of the 5th of January. I assure you all it is doing is asking you whether you wish to proceed and to let us know within a certain time. It also states that if you do not do so within that time, then the motion will be dismissed. My own view, for what it's worth, or my own suggestion to you, for what it's worth, is that it would be preferable for you to start with a fresh motion. So different now is the indictment to that which was originally filed, it would be much cleaner from your own point of view and from the Trial Chamber's point of view if you brought a fresh application so that we know precisely what the objection to the indictment is. That, however, is only a suggestion but it is one which I think you should take some note of. Now, are there any other matters that any party wishes to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just need to bring to the Court's attention at the first opportunity a document that was filed on the 10th of January by the Prosecutor entitled "Confidential Motion for Protective Measures," and I don't know if this should be done in public session or not. I'm going to talk about that motion a bit. I don't know if it's appropriate to do it in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ackerman, you have the advantage over me. I don't have that document. It hasn't found its way into any of the Judges' chambers. What is it, Mr. Keegan? Is it something that's likely to be of some dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Well, I would assume from Mr. Ackerman's posture that it probably will be, Your Honour. The motion, in essence, requests, I would say, what are the usual protective measures requested by the Prosecution at the beginning of any case, and in particular the confidentiality measures with respect to witnesses at this early stage of the proceedings. It was submitted yesterday to put the Defence on notice, because we have today the supportive materials for the amended indictment to provide to each counsel after this hearing, with the index. There's an attached letter again notifying of this motion and requesting that they respect the protective measures requested in the motion until such time as the Chamber has ruled on that motion. In light of that, the witness statements, as they will receive them, have identification material redacted until such time as there is a ruling by the Chamber. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems to me, Mr. Ackerman, it may be preferable for this to proceed in the usual way. You have a right to be heard, but it would be preferable, I think, if it was done in writing. It's a matter where there is usually, if there is any debate at all, a debate which will reveal, to some extent, the concerns which the Prosecution has. That should never be done in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't intend to do any such thing in public, and I have very little objection to what the Prosecutor -- or, in fact, no objection to what the Prosecutor characterises as the usual protective measures. However, this document contains some unusual language that I find a bit scurrilous and a bit offensive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ackerman, I think before you go any further, I don't have the document, you can't even refer me to a page or to a paragraph. If you have some objection to the language, I suggest that you either contact the Prosecution directly, which would probably be the best way, if it's something which can be cured. If it can't be cured, then you should put a response on and we'll deal with it in the usual way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm satisfied that no one can now claim that I didn't attempt to raise it at the first opportunity. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sure we have all been aware of that. Thank you. Is there anything else? All right, then. I'll treat this as a Status Conference for the purposes of the relevant Rule, and the time will commence to run again from today. I repeat that if anything arises which any party wishes to bring to the attention of the Trial Chamber, they may do so in the usual way. Thank you for your attendance.
